about.heading: About
about.description: This simulator visualizes how DOM events propagate through the Capturing → Target → Bubbling phases, step by step.

phases.heading: Event Phases
phases.capturingDesc: Event travels from window down to the target's parent.
phases.targetDesc: Event reaches the target element. All listeners fire regardless of useCapture.
phases.bubblingDesc: Event bubbles from target's parent back up to window.

concepts.heading: Key Concepts
concepts.stopPropagation: stopPropagation() — Prevents the event from reaching the next node.
concepts.stopImmediate: stopImmediatePropagation() — Also prevents remaining listeners on the same node.
concepts.preventDefault: preventDefault() — Cancels the browser's default behavior (e.g., form submission).
concepts.delegation: Event Delegation — Attaching a single listener to a parent to handle child events.

closureDashboard.title: Closure Simulator
closureDashboard.subtitle: Lexical Environment · Scope Chain · Memory Lifecycle

about.heading: About
about.description: This simulator visualizes how JavaScript closures work by showing the relationship between functions, their lexical environments, and memory lifecycle.

concepts.heading: Key Concepts
concepts.lexicalEnv: Lexical Environment — Each function creates an environment object that holds its local variables.
concepts.outerRef: Outer Reference — Every environment has a [[Outer]] pointer to its parent, forming the scope chain.
concepts.lifecycle: Memory Lifecycle — When a function returns, its environment stays in memory if a closure references it (retained). When no closures reference it, it becomes eligible for garbage collection.

statuses.heading: Environment Statuses
statuses.active: Active (green) — Currently on the call stack.
statuses.retained: Retained (amber) — Off the stack but kept alive by a closure.
statuses.collected: Collected (gray) — No references, eligible for GC.

about.heading: About
about.description: This simulator visualizes how the this keyword is dynamically bound in JavaScript depending on how a function is called.

rules.heading: 5 Binding Rules
rules.new: new Binding — When using new, a fresh object is created and bound as this.
rules.implicit: Implicit Binding — When calling obj.method(), the object before the dot becomes this.
rules.default: Default Binding — When calling a function standalone, this is undefined in strict mode.
rules.arrow: Arrow Function — Arrow functions don't have their own this; they inherit from the enclosing scope.
rules.lost: Lost Binding — When a method is extracted from its object (e.g., const fn = obj.method), this binding is lost.

keyInsight.heading: Key Insight
keyInsight.description: The same function can have different this values depending on how it is called — this is decided at call time, not definition time.

about.heading: About
about.description: This simulator visualizes how React's reconciliation algorithm compares Virtual DOM trees and computes the minimal set of DOM operations needed to update the UI.

algorithm.heading: Algorithm Steps
algorithm.step1: Render — When state changes, React calls the render function to produce a new Virtual DOM tree.
algorithm.step2: Diff — React compares the old and new trees. Same-type elements get prop updates; different types replace the entire subtree.
algorithm.step3: Key Matching — For lists, React uses key props to match old and new items efficiently, avoiding unnecessary re-creation.
algorithm.step4: Commit — React applies only the necessary DOM mutations (insertions, updates, deletions) in a single batch.

operations.heading: DOM Operations
operations.placement: A new node is inserted into the DOM.
operations.update: An existing node's props or text content are updated.
operations.deletion: A node is removed from the DOM.

keyInsight.heading: Key Insight
keyInsight.description: React's reconciliation is O(n) because it compares nodes level-by-level and uses keys for list items. Without keys, React falls back to index-based comparison which can cause unnecessary re-renders.
